verses.sanskrit: गान्धार्युवाच।पश्य माधव पुत्रान्मे शतसङ्ख्याञ्जितक्लमान्। गदया भीमसेनेन भूयिष्ठं निहतान्रणे॥१॥
इदं दुःखतरं मेऽद्य यदिमा मुक्तमूर्धजाः। हतपुत्रा रणे बालाः परिधावन्ति मे स्नुषाः॥२॥
verses.english: That which pains me more to-day is that these my young daughter-in-law, deprived of sons and with disheveled hairs, are wandering on the field today.

verses.sanskrit: प्रासादतलचारिण्यश्चरमैर्भूषणान्वितैः। अपन्ना यत्स्पृशन्तीमां रुधिरार्द्रां वसुन्धराम्॥३॥
verses.english: Alas, they who formerly walked only on the terraces of magnificent edifices with feet decorated with many ornaments, are now, in great misery, obliged to touch with those feet of theirs this hard Earth, covered with blood.

verses.sanskrit: कृच्छ्रादुत्सारयन्ति स्म गृध्रगोमायुवायसान्। दुःखेनार्ता विघूर्णन्त्यो मत्ता इव चरन्त्युत॥४॥
verses.english: Reeling in sorrow, they are moving about like drunk persons, driving away with difficulty vulture and jackals and crows.

verses.sanskrit: एषाऽन्या त्वनवद्याङ्गी करसम्मितमध्यमा। घोरमायोधनं दृष्ट्वा निपतत्यतिदुःखिता॥५॥
दृष्ट्वा मे पार्थिवसुतामेतां लक्ष्मणमातरम्। राजपुत्रीं महाबाहो मनो न ह्युपशाम्यति॥६॥
verses.english: Beholding this princess, this mother of Lakshmana, O you of mighty-arms, my heart is torn with sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रातॄंश्चान्याः पितॄंश्चान्याः पुत्रांश्च निहतान्भुवि। दृष्ट्वा परिपतन्त्येषाः प्रगृह्य सुमहाभुजान्॥७॥
मध्यमानां तु नारीणां वृद्धानां चापराजित। आक्रन्दं हतबन्धूनां दारुणे वैशसे शृणु॥८॥
verses.english: Hear, O unvanquished one, the loud lamentations of those elderly ladies and those others of middle age on witnessing this terrible destruction.

verses.sanskrit: रथनीडानि देहांश्च हतानां गजवाजिनाम्। आश्रित्य श्रममोहार्ताः स्थिताः पश्य महाभुज॥९॥
verses.english: See, O you of great might, those dames, exhausted with fatigue, are taking rest, supporting themselves against broken boxes of cars and the bodies of slain elephants and steeds.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यां चापहृतं कायाच्चारुकुण्डलमुन्नसम्। स्वस्य बन्धोः शिरः कृष्ण गृहीत्वा पश्य तिष्ठतीम्॥१०॥
verses.english: See, O Krishna, taking up some relative's severed head adorned with beautiful nose and ear-rings, some one amongst them, is standing sorrowfully.

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वजातिकृतं पापं मन्ये नाल्पमिवानघ। एताभिर्निरवद्याभिर्मया चैवाल्यमेधया॥११॥
verses.english: I think, O sinless one, they and myself of little understanding must have perpetrated great iniquities in our previous lives, since, O Janarddana, all our relatives and kinsmen have thus been killed by king Yudhishthira. Our acts, fair or unfair, must bear fruits, O you of Vrishni's race.

verses.sanskrit: यदिदं धर्मराजेन पातितं नो जनार्दन। न हि नाशोऽस्ति वार्ष्णेय कर्मणोः शुभपापयोः॥१२॥
प्रत्यग्रवयसः पश्य दर्शनीयकुचाननाः। कुलेषु जाता ह्रीमत्यः कृष्णपक्ष्माक्षिमूर्धजाः॥१३॥
verses.english: See, O Madhava, those young ladies having beautiful breasts and abdomen, born in respectable families, of great modesty, having black eye-lashes and tresses of the same color on their heads, having voice sweet and dear like that of swans, are falling down, unconscious from great grief and crying piteously like fights of cranes.

verses.sanskrit: हंसगद्गदभाषिण्यो दुःखशोकप्रमोहिताः। सारस्य इव वाशन्त्यः पतिताः पश्य माधव॥१४॥
फुल्लपद्मप्रकाशानि पुण्डरीकाक्षयोषिताम्। अनवद्यानि वक्त्राणि तापयत्येष रश्मिवान्॥१५॥
verses.english: See, O lotus-eyed, hero, there beautiful faces resembling full-blown lotuses, scorched by the sun.

verses.sanskrit: ईर्षूणां मम पुत्राणां वासुदेवावरोधनम्। मत्तमातङ्गदर्पाणां पश्यन्त्यद्य पृथग्जनाः॥१६॥
शतचन्द्राणि चर्माणि ध्वजांश्चादित्यवर्चसः। रौक्माणि चैव वर्माणि निष्कानपि च काञ्चनान्॥१७॥
शिरस्त्राणानि चैतानि पुत्राणां मे महीतले। पश्य दीप्तानि गोविन्द पावकान्सुहुतानिव॥१८॥
एष दुःशासनः शेते शूरेणामित्रघातिना। पीतशोणितसर्वाङ्गो युधि भीमेन पातितः॥१९॥
verses.english: There, Dusshasana sleep, killed by Bhima, having the blood of all his limbs drunk by that heroic slayer of foes.

verses.sanskrit: गदया भीमसेनेन पश्य माधव मे सुतम्। द्यूतक्लेशाननुस्मृत्य द्रौपदीनोदितेन च॥२०॥
verses.english: Look at that other son of mine, O Madhava, killed by Bhima with his mace, actuated by Draupadi and the memory of his woes at the time of the match at dice.

verses.sanskrit: उक्ता ह्यनेन पाञ्चाली सभायां द्यूतनिर्जिता। प्रियं चिकीर्षता भ्रातुः कर्णस्य च जनार्दन॥२१॥
verses.english: Addressing the princess of Panchala, in the midst of the assembly, who had been won by dice, this Dusshasana, desirous of pleasing his (elder) brother and Karna, O Janarddana, had said,-You are now the wife of a slave! With Sahadeva and Nakula and Arjuna, O lady, enter our household now.

verses.sanskrit: सहैव सहदेवेन नकुलेनार्जुनेन च। दासीभूताऽसि पाञ्चालि क्षिप्रं प्रविश नो गृहान्॥२२॥
ततोऽहमब्रुवं कृष्ण तदा दुर्योधनं नृपम्। मृत्युपाशपरिक्षिप्तं शकुनिं पुत्र वर्जय॥२३॥
निबोधैनं सुदुर्बुद्धिं मातुलं कलहप्रियम्। क्षिप्रमेनं परित्यज्य पुत्र शाम्यस्व पाण्डवैः॥२४॥
verses.english: Know your maternal uncle to be very wicked and greatly fond of quarrel. Discard him forthwith and make peace with the Pandavas, O son.

verses.sanskrit: न बुद्ध्यसे त्वं दुर्बुद्धे भीमसेनममर्षणम्। वाङ्गराचैस्तुदंस्तीक्ष्णैरुल्काभिरिव कुञ्जरम्॥२५॥
तानेवं रहसि क्रुद्धो वाक्शल्यानवधारयन्। उत्ससर्ज विषं तेषु सर्पो गोवृषभेष्विव॥२६॥
verses.english: Alas, neglecting my wordy, he vomited his poison of words at them, who had already been cut with wordy arrows, like a snake vomiting his poison at a bull.

verses.sanskrit: एष दुःशासनः शेते विक्षिप्य विपुलौ भुजौ। निहतो भीमसेनेन सिंहेनेव महागजः॥२७॥
verses.english: there that Dusshasana sleeps stretching his tow massive arms, killed by Bhimasena like a powerful elephant by a lion.

verses.sanskrit: अत्यर्थमकरोद्रौद्रं भीमसेनोऽत्यमर्षणः। दुःशासनस्य यत्क्रुद्धोऽपिबच्छोणितमाहवे॥२८॥
verses.english: The very angry Bhimasena perpetrated a most dreadful deed by drinking in battle the blood of his foes.
